title: OpenBSD 8.0 Brings Expanded Hardware Support, Security Enhancements, and Virtualization Improvements
gist: OpenBSD 8.0 expands the AMD64 kernel virtual address space from 4 GB to 512 GB, adds up-to-64-vCPU guests in vmm/vmd, Intel Arc A-Series GPU support, RISC-V vector extension support and arm64 hibernation, and ships LibreSSL 4.4.0 and OpenSSH 10.6. NVIDIA GPUs remain unsupported and the lack of ZFS/Btrfs keeps it a poor fit for large servers.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0 expands the AMD64 kernel virtual address space from 4 GB to 512 GB, enabling it to map graphics cards with more than 4 GB of VRAM.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Niche OS catching up to modern GPU memory sizes; no direct market impact.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0's vmm/vmd hypervisor now supports multi-processor virtual machines with up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Makes OpenBSD's native hypervisor more viable for real workloads, still marginal versus KVM/commercial hypervisors.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0 expands RISC-V support including the 'V' vector extension and Advanced Interrupt Architecture, plus SpacemiT K3 SoC and PCIe controller drivers.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Continued OS-level RISC-V enablement is a small signal of ecosystem maturation for RISC-V silicon.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0 adds Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) GPU support but NVIDIA GPUs remain unsupported, partly because NVIDIA does not provide proprietary binary drivers for OpenBSD as it does for Linux and FreeBSD.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Illustrates NVIDIA's driver ecosystem as a gatekeeper of OS-level GPU support.

themes.theme: Security track record and crypto stack

insights.claim: The OpenBSD project claims more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Security pedigree underpins OpenBSD's role in firewalls/network appliances and its spinoffs (OpenSSH, LibreSSL).
insights.quote: We remain proud of OpenBSD's record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0 ships OpenSSH 10.6, which disables LZ77 SSH compression and rejects $ and \ characters in command-line usernames to mitigate potential shell injection, plus LibreSSL 4.4.0 with compatibility fixes especially for Windows.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: OpenSSH changes propagate to virtually every Linux/Unix fleet; watch downstream distro updates.

insights.claim: A longtime OpenBSD user notes it is extremely stable across upgrades but may not suit large servers because it lacks advanced filesystems such as ZFS, Btrfs or GeFS.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Confirms OpenBSD stays a niche security/network OS rather than a general server platform.
